newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rio state, federal government to sign debt deal today.
newsitem.headline: Rio state, federal government to sign debt deal today.

text.p: Rio de Janeiro state and federal officials will sign a deal at 1500 local (1700 GMT) to refinance 11.3 billion reais of debts owed by the state, Rio officials said.
Under the terms of the deal the state government will repay its debts to the central government over 30 years and has agreed to retire 20 percent of its debt stock through selling off assets.
Newspapers said the state government will pay annual interest rates of 6.0 or 7.5 percent, depending on the guarantees it presents to pay off 20 percent of the debt.
If it raises only 10 percent of its debt through asset sales, it will pay interest of 7.5 percent, newspapers said.
The accord, which still has to be approved by the Senate, is key to allow the publication of new bid specifications for the sale of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj.
The tender document may be published later this month.
Banerj, whose sell-off has been postponed twice due to court rulings, is the first Brazilian state bank to be privatised.
